rationale:
The supplied 9-step proof has three separable obligations. The split has three independent children with no sibling dependencies.

1. Steps 1–3: zero extension identifies CF_N(U) with C_c(↥U, ℝ^N) and turns L into a locally bounded linear L′ with L f = L′(f∘ι). This is smr_rb_transfer_functional.
2. Steps 4–7: Simon 1.4.14 with the Carathéodory measure and field replaced by a Borel measure, finite on compacts, and a Borel field with norm ≤ 1 everywhere and = 1 a.e., on any σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff Y. This is a reusable Borel form of the Riesz theorem: smr_rb_borel_riesz_sigma_compact.
3. Steps 1 and 8–9: push the Borel data forward from ↥U to ℝ^P, with integrability and the integral identity. This is smr_rb_pushforward_subtype.

Parent assembly (kernel-checked):
- Obtain L′ from child 1.
- Set LocallyCompactSpace ↥U := hU.locallyCompactSpace. SigmaCompactSpace ↥U is then inferred from second countability, and BorelSpace ↥U is Subtype.borelSpace.
- Apply child 2 at Y := ↥U to get m and ν₁.
- Apply child 3 to get μ, ν and all their properties.
- For f ∈ CF_N(U), take g from child 1 and chain L f = L′ g = ∫⟨g, ν₁⟩dm = ∫⟨f∘ι, ν₁⟩dm = ∫⟨f, ν⟩dμ. Integrability comes from child 3.

subproblems.title: Zero extension turns a locally bounded functional on CF_N(U) into a locally bounded linear functional on C_c(↥U, ℝ^N)
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, H := ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), and L : (ℝ^P → H) → ℝ be additive and homogeneous on CF_N(U) := {f : ℝ^P → H continuous, compactly supported, tsupport f ⊆ U} (L(f + g) = L f + L g and L(c • f) = c · L f for f, g ∈ CF_N(U), c ∈ ℝ) and locally bounded above (for every compact K ⊆ U there is B with L(f) ≤ B for every continuous f with tsupport f ⊆ K and ‖f(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x). Let Y := ↥U (U with the subspace topology) and ι : Y → ℝ^P the inclusion. Then there is an ℝ-linear map L′ : C_c(Y, H) → ℝ such that (a) for every compact K_Y ⊆ Y there is B ∈ ℝ with L′(g) ≤ B for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H) with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and tsupport g ⊆ K_Y, and (b) for every f ∈ CF_N(U) there is g ∈ C_c(Y, H) with g(y) = f(ι y) for all y ∈ Y and L(f) = L′(g).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ L : (Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) → ℝ, (∀ f g : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → L (f + g) = L f + L g) → (∀ (c : ℝ) (f : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → L (c • f) = c * L f) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ f : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Continuous f → tsupport f ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ 1) → L f ≤ B) → ∃ L' : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ↥U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ K : Set ↥U, IsCompact K → ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ↥U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → tsupport g ⊆ K → L' g ≤ B) ∧ ∀ f : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → ∃ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ↥U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ y : ↥U, g y = f ↑y) ∧ L f = L' g
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); CF_N(U) := {f : ℝ^P → H : f continuous, HasCompactSupport f, tsupport f ⊆ U}. Y := ↥U is U with the subspace topology (Hausdorff, as a subspace of ℝ^P) and ι := Subtype.val : Y → ℝ^P is the inclusion; C_c(Y, H) = CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y H with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. This is the topological part of step 1 and steps 2–3 (including the converse half of step 2) of the parent proof of smr_riesz_borel_euclidean, written out in full.

0. (Extension by zero.) For g ∈ C_c(Y, H) define ĝ : ℝ^P → H by ĝ(x) := g(⟨x, hx⟩) if hx : x ∈ U, and ĝ(x) := 0 if x ∉ U. (In Lean ĝ = Function.extend Subtype.val g 0: it equals g ⟨x, hx⟩ for x ∈ U by Function.extend_val_apply, and 0 for x ∉ U by Function.extend_apply', because a point x ∉ U is not of the form ι y.)

1. (Pointwise bound.) If ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y ∈ Y, then ‖ĝ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P: for x ∈ U, ‖ĝ(x)‖ = ‖g(⟨x, hx⟩)‖ ≤ 1; for x ∉ U, ‖ĝ(x)‖ = ‖0‖ = 0 ≤ 1.

2. (Support of ĝ.) Put C_g := ι(tsupport g). As g has compact support, tsupport g is compact, so C_g is compact (continuous image of a compact set) and hence closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P. If ĝ(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ U (otherwise ĝ(x) = 0) and g(⟨x, hx⟩) ≠ 0, so x = ι⟨x, hx⟩ ∈ ι(support g) ⊆ C_g. Thus support ĝ ⊆ C_g and, C_g being closed, tsupport ĝ = closure(support ĝ) ⊆ C_g. Consequently (a) tsupport ĝ is a closed subset of the compact set C_g, so ĝ has compact support; (b) tsupport ĝ ⊆ C_g ⊆ U, since every point of C_g has the form ι y ∈ U. (Mathlib: HasCompactSupport.tsupport_extend_zero_subset and HasCompactSupport.extend_zero, applied with continuous_subtype_val.)

3. (Continuity of ĝ.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P. If x ∉ tsupport ĝ, then the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport ĝ is a neighbourhood of x on which ĝ vanishes identically, so ĝ is continuous at x. If x ∈ tsupport ĝ, then x ∈ U by step 2(b). Since U is open, ι is an open embedding, so continuity of ĝ at x = ι⟨x, hx⟩ is equivalent to continuity of ĝ ∘ ι at ⟨x, hx⟩; and ĝ ∘ ι = g (step 0) is continuous. Hence ĝ is continuous (Mathlib: HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero, which uses IsOpen U). With step 2, ĝ ∈ CF_N(U) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H).

4. (The extension is linear.) For g, h ∈ C_c(Y, H) and c ∈ ℝ we have (g + h)^ = ĝ + ĥ and (c • g)^ = c • ĝ as functions ℝ^P → H: for x ∈ U both sides evaluate to g(⟨x, hx⟩) + h(⟨x, hx⟩), respectively c • g(⟨x, hx⟩); for x ∉ U both sides evaluate to 0 = 0 + 0, respectively 0 = c • 0.

5. (Definition and linearity of L′.) Define L′(g) := L(ĝ) for g ∈ C_c(Y, H). By step 4, L′(g + h) = L(ĝ + ĥ); since ĝ, ĥ ∈ CF_N(U) (steps 2–3), the additivity hypothesis gives L(ĝ + ĥ) = L(ĝ) + L(ĥ) = L′(g) + L′(h). Likewise L′(c • g) = L(c • ĝ) = c · L(ĝ) = c · L′(g) by the homogeneity hypothesis, applicable because ĝ ∈ CF_N(U). Hence L′ : C_c(Y, H) → ℝ is ℝ-linear.

6. (Local bound for L′; first conjunct.) Let K_Y ⊆ Y be compact. Then K := ι(K_Y) is compact (continuous image) and K ⊆ U. The local boundedness hypothesis gives B ∈ ℝ with L(f) ≤ B for every continuous f : ℝ^P → H with tsupport f ⊆ K and ‖f(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x. Let g ∈ C_c(Y, H) with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and tsupport g ⊆ K_Y. Then ĝ is continuous (step 3), tsupport ĝ ⊆ ι(tsupport g) ⊆ ι(K_Y) = K (step 2 and monotonicity of images), and ‖ĝ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x (step 1). Therefore L′(g) = L(ĝ) ≤ B. This single B serves for all such g.

7. (Restricting f ∈ CF_N(U) to Y.) Let f ∈ CF_N(U) and K′ := ι⁻¹(tsupport f) ⊆ Y. The set tsupport f is compact and contained in U = range ι, and ι is an inducing map (a topological embedding); for an inducing map and a subset S of its range, ι⁻¹(S) is compact iff S is compact (Topology.IsInducing.isCompact_preimage_iff). So K′ is compact. The map f ∘ ι : Y → H is continuous (composition of continuous maps) and vanishes outside K′: if y ∉ K′ then ι y ∉ tsupport f, hence f(ι y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). As Y is Hausdorff, a function vanishing outside a compact set has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro). Let g ∈ C_c(Y, H) be f ∘ ι bundled with these facts; by construction g(y) = f(ι y) for every y ∈ Y.

8. (ĝ = f, hence L(f) = L′(g); second conjunct.) For x ∈ U, ĝ(x) = g(⟨x, hx⟩) = f(x). For x ∉ U, ĝ(x) = 0, and x ∉ tsupport f because tsupport f ⊆ U, so f(x) = 0 = ĝ(x). Hence ĝ = f and L(f) = L(ĝ) = L′(g).

9. (Conclusion.) L′ from step 5 satisfies the local bound of step 6, and for every f ∈ CF_N(U) the element g of step 7 satisfies g(y) = f(ι y) for all y and L(f) = L′(g) (step 8). This is exactly the assertion. ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument): the statement uses only names visible after import GMT.Ch06.Submission; no extra import is needed for this child. Define E g := Function.extend Subtype.val (⇑g) 0 and build L′ as a LinearMap record {toFun := fun g => L (E g), map_add' := …, map_smul' := …}; the pointwise identities of step 4 follow from Function.extend_val_apply / Function.extend_apply' with CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.coe_add / coe_smul. A scratch Lean proof following exactly these steps was kernel-checked against the frozen submission (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
proof_key_steps: Extend g ∈ C_c(↥U, H) by zero to ĝ = Function.extend Subtype.val g 0; ĝ = g on U and 0 off U, and ‖g‖ ≤ 1 implies ‖ĝ‖ ≤ 1.
tsupport ĝ ⊆ ι(tsupport g), a compact (hence closed) subset of U; so ĝ has compact support with tsupport in U.
ĝ is continuous since U is open (HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero); hence ĝ ∈ CF_N(U).
g ↦ ĝ is additive and homogeneous pointwise, so L′(g) := L(ĝ) is ℝ-linear by the additivity/homogeneity of L on CF_N(U).
For compact K_Y ⊆ ↥U use the bound B for K = ι(K_Y): tsupport ĝ ⊆ ι(tsupport g) ⊆ K and ‖ĝ‖ ≤ 1 give L′(g) ≤ B.
For f ∈ CF_N(U), g := f ∘ ι has compact support (ι⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact as tsupport f ⊆ range ι), g y = f ↑y, and ĝ = f, so L f = L′ g.

subproblems.title: Riesz representation (Simon 1.4.14) with a Borel measure and a Borel unit field on a σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff space
subproblems.statement: Let Y be a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, N ∈ ℕ, H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), and L : C_c(Y, H) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map such that for every compact K ⊆ Y there is B ∈ ℝ with L(g) ≤ B for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H) with ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and tsupport g ⊆ K. Then there are a (Borel) measure m on Y and a Borel measurable ν : Y → H such that m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y, ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y, and L(g) = ∫_Y ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dm(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Y : Type) [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y] [SigmaCompactSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y] (N : ℕ) (L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set Y, IsCompact K → ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → tsupport g ⊆ K → L g ≤ B) → ∃ (m : Measure Y) (ν : Y → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ K : Set Y, IsCompact K → m K < ∞) ∧ Measurable ν ∧ (∀ y, ‖ν y‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ᵐ y ∂m, ‖ν y‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), L g = ∫ y, inner ℝ (g y) (ν y) ∂m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. Y is a Hausdorff, locally compact, σ-compact topological space whose σ-algebra is its Borel σ-algebra ([MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y], so measurable = Borel); H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), a finite-dimensional real inner product space, second countable, with its Borel σ-algebra; C_c(Y, H) = CompactlySupportedContinuousMap Y H. Outer-measure notions follow Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01 (Simon, Ch. 1): a set A is Carathéodory measurable for an outer measure μ₀ if μ₀(T) = μ₀(T ∩ A) + μ₀(T ∖ A) for all T. This is steps 4–7 of the parent proof of smr_riesz_borel_euclidean (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 together with the completion/Borel-modification argument), stated for a general σ-compact locally compact Hausdorff space Y; the parent applies it to Y = ↥U.

1. (Riesz hypothesis.) For every compact K ⊆ Y the number B provided by the hypothesis is an upper bound of the set L''{g ∈ C_c(Y, H) : (∀ y, ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1) ∧ tsupport g ⊆ K}. Thus L satisfies Simon's local boundedness hypothesis of Ch. 1, 4.14 (IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L).

2. (Riesz representation, Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14.) Since Y is locally compact Hausdorff and H is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14 gives an outer measure μ₀ on Y with hμ₀ : IsRadonOuterMeasure μ₀ and a map ν₀ : Y → H such that (i) ν₀ is measurable from the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀ to the Borel σ-algebra of H; (ii) ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 for μ_C-a.e. y; (iii) L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ_C(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H). Here μ_C := hμ₀.toCaratheodoryMeasure is μ₀ regarded as a measure on its Carathéodory σ-algebra. From IsRadonOuterMeasure we use: Borel regularity (every Borel set is Carathéodory measurable, and every A ⊆ Y has a Borel hull B ⊇ A with μ₀(B) = μ₀(A)), and finiteness on compact sets (μ₀(K) < ∞ for compact K). Moreover μ_C(A) = μ₀(A) for every A ⊆ Y (IsRadonOuterMeasure.toCaratheodoryMeasure_apply_all).

3. (The Borel measure m.) The σ-algebra of Y is the Borel σ-algebra, which is contained in the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ₀ (Borel regularity). Let m be the restriction of μ₀ to it, i.e. the measure m(A) = μ₀(A) for measurable A (m := μ₀.toMeasure hle with hle : Borel ≤ Carathéodory; this is hμ₀.borel_regular.toBorelMeasure). Claim: m(A) = μ₀(A) for every A ⊆ Y. Indeed m(A) ≥ μ₀(A), because the measure induced by an outer measure dominates it on all sets (le_toMeasure_apply); and if B ⊇ A is a Borel hull with μ₀(B) = μ₀(A), then m(A) ≤ m(B) = μ₀(B) = μ₀(A). Consequences:
(a) m(K) = μ₀(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y.
(b) For every A ⊆ Y: m(A) = 0 ⟺ μ₀(A) = 0 ⟺ μ_C(A) = 0. As "Q holds a.e." means that the set where Q fails has measure 0, a property holds m-a.e. if and only if it holds μ_C-a.e.
(c) The trim of μ_C to the σ-algebra of Y equals m: for every Borel A, (μ_C.trim hle)(A) = μ_C(A) = μ₀(A) = m(A), and two measures agreeing on all measurable sets are equal.

4. (Carathéodory-measurable sets are m-null-measurable.) Write Y = ⋃_n K_n with K_n compact (σ-compactness). By local compactness each K_n has an open neighbourhood V_n with compact closure, and μ₀(V_n) ≤ μ₀(closure V_n) < ∞. Hence Y is covered by countably many open sets of finite μ₀-measure, i.e. μ₀ is open-σ-finite (isOpenSigmaFinite_of_finite_compacts hμ₀.finite_compacts). By IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.exists_borel_subset_mod_null, every Carathéodory-measurable A ⊆ Y contains a Borel set B with μ₀(A ∖ B) = 0. Then A = B ∪ (A ∖ B), where B is measurable and m(A ∖ B) = μ₀(A ∖ B) = 0 by step 3; a union of a measurable set and an m-null set is m-null-measurable, so A is m-null-measurable.

5. (A Borel version of ν₀.) For every Borel S ⊆ H, the set ν₀⁻¹(S) is Carathéodory measurable (step 2(i)), hence m-null-measurable (step 4); so ν₀ is m-null-measurable. Since H is second countable, its Borel σ-algebra is countably generated, and a null-measurable map into a countably generated measurable space is almost everywhere measurable (MeasureTheory.NullMeasurable.aemeasurable). Hence there is a Borel measurable ν₀′ : Y → H with ν₀(y) = ν₀′(y) for m-a.e. y.

6. (Normalized Borel field.) Define ν(y) := ν₀′(y) if ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1, and ν(y) := 0 otherwise. The set {y : ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1} is Borel (ν₀′ and the norm are measurable), so ν is Borel measurable. For every y, ‖ν(y)‖ equals ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1 or ‖0‖ = 0, so ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1. By step 2(ii) and step 3(b), ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y. For m-a.e. y both ν₀(y) = ν₀′(y) and ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 1 hold; for such y we get ‖ν₀′(y)‖ = 1, hence ν(y) = ν₀′(y) = ν₀(y) and ‖ν(y)‖ = 1. Thus ‖ν‖ = 1 m-a.e. and ν₀ = ν m-a.e.; by step 3(b) also ν₀ = ν μ_C-a.e. (the exceptional set {y : ν₀(y) ≠ ν(y)} is m-null, hence μ_C-null).

7. (Representation with Borel data.) Let g ∈ C_c(Y, H) and F(y) := ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩. F is Borel measurable, since y ↦ (g(y), ν(y)) is measurable (g is continuous, hence Borel; ν is Borel) and the inner product H × H → ℝ is continuous, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra, which equals the Borel σ-algebra of H × H because H is second countable; F is real valued, hence strongly measurable for the σ-algebra of Y. Therefore
L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν₀(y)⟩ dμ_C(y)   (step 2(iii))
     = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dμ_C(y)    (the integrands agree μ_C-a.e. by step 6)
     = ∫ F d(μ_C.trim hle)        (integral_trim, F being strongly measurable for the smaller σ-algebra)
     = ∫ F dm                     (step 3(c)).

8. (Conclusion.) The pair (m, ν) satisfies: m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y (step 3(a)); ν is measurable (step 6); ‖ν(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y (step 6); and L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩ dm(y) for every g ∈ C_c(Y, H) (step 7). (No case distinction is needed for N = 0: then H = {0}, so ‖ν₀(y)‖ = 0 for every y and step 2(ii) forces μ_C(Y) = 0, hence m = 0 by step 3(b); all assertions still follow from steps 2–7.) ∎

proof_key_steps: The hypothesis gives IsLocallyBoundedCcFunctional L; apply simon_theorem_4_14 to get a Radon outer measure μ₀, its Carathéodory measure μ_C and a Carathéodory-measurable ν₀ with ‖ν₀‖ = 1 μ_C-a.e. and L g = ∫⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ_C.
Let m be μ₀ restricted to the Borel σ-algebra of Y; Borel hulls give m(A) = μ₀(A) = μ_C(A) for all A ⊆ Y, so m is finite on compacts, m and μ_C have the same null sets, and μ_C.trim = m.
σ-compactness makes μ₀ open-σ-finite, so each Carathéodory-measurable set is a Borel set plus a μ₀-null set, hence m-null-measurable; thus ν₀ is m-null-measurable.
H is second countable, so ν₀ is m-a.e. equal to a Borel ν₀′ (NullMeasurable.aemeasurable); set ν := ν₀′ where ‖ν₀′‖ = 1 and 0 elsewhere: ν Borel, ‖ν‖ ≤ 1, ν = ν₀ and ‖ν‖ = 1 m-a.e. and μ_C-a.e.
L g = ∫⟨g, ν₀⟩ dμ_C = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ_C = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ d(μ_C.trim) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dm by integral_congr_ae and integral_trim.

subproblems.title: Push-forward of Borel representing data from the open subspace ↥U to ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, Y := ↥U with the subspace topology and subspace (Borel) σ-algebra, ι : Y → ℝ^P the inclusion, H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), m a measure on Y with m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y, and ν₁ : Y → H measurable with ‖ν₁(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and ‖ν₁(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y. Then there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^P and a Borel map ν : ℝ^P → H such that μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ‖ν(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, ‖ν(x)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. x, and for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → H with tsupport f ⊆ U the function x ↦ ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ is μ-integrable and ∫ ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ(x) = ∫_Y ⟨f(ι y), ν₁(y)⟩ dm(y).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (m : Measure ↥U) (ν₁ : ↥U → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ K : Set ↥U, IsCompact K → m K < ∞) → Measurable ν₁ → (∀ y, ‖ν₁ y‖ ≤ 1) → (∀ᵐ y ∂m, ‖ν₁ y‖ = 1) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ν : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), Measurable ν ∧ μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ x, ‖ν x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖ν x‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ f : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (f x) (ν x)) μ ∧ ∫ x, inner ℝ (f x) (ν x) ∂μ = ∫ y, inner ℝ (f ↑y) (ν₁ y) ∂m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); Y := ↥U is U with the subspace topology and the subspace σ-algebra (the comap of the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P under ι := Subtype.val : Y → ℝ^P; it is the Borel σ-algebra of Y); CF_N(U) := {f : ℝ^P → H : f continuous, HasCompactSupport f, tsupport f ⊆ U}. Hypotheses: m is a measure on Y with m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Y, and ν₁ : Y → H is measurable with ‖ν₁(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y and ‖ν₁(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y. This is step 1 (measurable embedding) and steps 8–9 of the parent proof of smr_riesz_borel_euclidean, written out in full.

1. (ι is a measurable embedding.) ι is injective; it is measurable because the σ-algebra of Y is the comap σ-algebra; and it maps measurable sets to measurable sets: a measurable set of Y has the form ι⁻¹(S) with S Borel, and ι(ι⁻¹(S)) = S ∩ U is Borel because U is open, hence Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe hU.measurableSet). For a measurable embedding ι and μ := m.map ι the following hold: μ(A) = m(ι⁻¹(A)) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply); ∫ F dμ = ∫_Y F(ι y) dm(y) for every F : ℝ^P → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map); and a property Q holds μ-a.e. iff Q ∘ ι holds m-a.e. (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff).

2. (Definitions.) Let μ := m.map ι, a measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P, and let ν be the extension of ν₁ by zero: ν(x) := ν₁(⟨x, hx⟩) if hx : x ∈ U, and ν(x) := 0 if x ∉ U (in Lean ν = Function.extend Subtype.val ν₁ 0). Then ν(ι y) = ν₁(y) for every y ∈ Y (ι is injective), and ν(x) = 0 for every x ∉ U (such x is not of the form ι y).

3. (ν is Borel.) For a Borel set S ⊆ H we have ν⁻¹(S) = ι(ν₁⁻¹(S)) ∪ E_S, where E_S := ℝ^P ∖ U if 0 ∈ S and E_S := ∅ otherwise. The set ι(ν₁⁻¹(S)) is Borel because ν₁⁻¹(S) is measurable in Y and ι maps measurable sets to measurable sets (step 1), and ℝ^P ∖ U is closed. Hence ν is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend, with the measurable extension value 0).

4. (‖ν‖ ≤ 1 everywhere.) For x ∈ U, ‖ν(x)‖ = ‖ν₁(⟨x, hx⟩)‖ ≤ 1 by hypothesis; for x ∉ U, ‖ν(x)‖ = ‖0‖ = 0 ≤ 1.

5. (μ lives on U.) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = m(ι⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ U)) = m(∅) = 0, because every ι y lies in U.

6. (Local finiteness.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. Since K ⊆ U = range ι and ι is a topological embedding (inducing), ι⁻¹(K) is compact in Y (Topology.IsInducing.isCompact_preimage_iff). Hence μ(K) = m(ι⁻¹(K)) < ∞ by the hypothesis on m.

7. (‖ν‖ = 1 μ-a.e.) By step 1 this is equivalent to ‖ν(ι y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y; since ν(ι y) = ν₁(y) (step 2), this is exactly the hypothesis ‖ν₁(y)‖ = 1 for m-a.e. y.

8. (Integrability.) Let f ∈ CF_N(U) and F(x) := ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩. F is Borel measurable: x ↦ (f(x), ν(x)) is measurable (f is continuous, ν is Borel by step 3) and the inner product H × H → ℝ is continuous, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra, which equals the Borel σ-algebra of H × H because H is second countable; in particular F is a.e. strongly measurable. F vanishes outside T := tsupport f: if x ∉ T then f(x) = 0 and hence F(x) = 0, so support F ⊆ T. The set T is compact (f has compact support), so the continuous function f is bounded on T: there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C for x ∈ T. For x ∈ T, |F(x)| ≤ ‖f(x)‖ ‖ν(x)‖ ≤ ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C, by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and step 4. Since T ⊆ U is compact, μ(T) < ∞ by step 6. A measurable function bounded by C almost everywhere on a set of finite measure is integrable on that set (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), so F is μ-integrable on T; as support F ⊆ T, F is μ-integrable on ℝ^P (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).

9. (Integral identity.) By step 1 (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map) and step 2,
∫ ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ(x) = ∫_Y ⟨f(ι y), ν(ι y)⟩ dm(y) = ∫_Y ⟨f(ι y), ν₁(y)⟩ dm(y).

10. (Conclusion.) The pair (μ, ν) satisfies: ν is measurable (step 3); μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (step 5); μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (step 6); ‖ν(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x (step 4); ‖ν(x)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. x (step 7); and for every f ∈ CF_N(U), x ↦ ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ is μ-integrable (step 8) with ∫ ⟨f(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ(x) = ∫_Y ⟨f(ι y), ν₁(y)⟩ dm(y) (step 9). ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument): the statement and the proof only need names visible after import GMT.Ch06.Submission. Useful API: MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe hU.measurableSet; Subtype.val_injective.extend_apply; Function.extend_apply'; MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend; MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply; MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff; MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; Topology.IsInducing.subtypeVal.isCompact_preimage_iff; IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded; ae_restrict_mem; integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset; norm_inner_le_norm; measurability of x ↦ inner ℝ (f x) (ν x) as continuous_inner.measurable.comp (hf.measurable.prodMk hν). A scratch Lean proof following exactly these steps was kernel-checked against the frozen submission (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
proof_key_steps: ι = Subtype.val : ↥U → ℝ^P is a measurable embedding (U open), so μ := m.map ι satisfies μ(A) = m(ι⁻¹A), ∫ F dμ = ∫ F ∘ ι dm and μ-a.e. ⟺ m-a.e. after composing with ι.
ν := Function.extend Subtype.val ν₁ 0 is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend), ν ∘ ι = ν₁, ν = 0 off U, and ‖ν‖ ≤ 1.
μ(Uᶜ) = m(∅) = 0; for compact K ⊆ U, ι⁻¹K is compact, so μ(K) = m(ι⁻¹K) < ∞; ‖ν‖ = 1 μ-a.e. by ae_map_iff and ν ∘ ι = ν₁.
For f ∈ CF_N(U), ⟨f, ν⟩ is Borel, bounded by sup‖f‖ on the compact T = tsupport f ⊆ U of finite μ-measure and zero off T, hence μ-integrable.
∫⟨f, ν⟩ dμ = ∫⟨f ∘ ι, ν ∘ ι⟩ dm = ∫⟨f ↑y, ν₁ y⟩ dm(y) by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map.
